etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English stop.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism), derived from talent. Compare Korean 탤런트 (taelleonteu).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English down.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Learned borrowing from Latin vīrus.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English form.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English foam.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English plan.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English monitor.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 上(うわ) (uwa-, the 被(ひ)覆(ふく)形(けい) (hifukukei, “bound form”) of 上(うえ) (ue, “up; top”)) + 回(まわ)る (mawaru, “to go around; to prevail”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Its Heian Kyoto accent pattern LF implies this is the same as 終(しゅう)止(し)形(けい) (shūshikei, “conclusive form”) of the verb 勝(か)つ (katsu, “to win”), which has low tone L-. Note the existence of Classical Japanese かつ (katsu, “to be bearable”), homophone of its classical potential form which might have the sense "capable of opposing". Possibly related to 片(かた) (kata, “one of a pair”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 余所(よそ) (yoso, “elsewhere; others”) + 見(み) (mi, “looking”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Uncertain. First attested in Japanese in 1929. Might be a borrowing from written Chinese 動向, or possibly a coinage within Japanese of Middle Chinese-derived elements as a compound of 動 (dō, “moving, movement”) + 向 (kō, “facing, direction”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Compound of 名(な) (na, “name”) + 高(たか)い (takai, “high, lofty”).
The takai changes to dakai as an instance of rendaku (連濁).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Originally from Middle Chinese 塾 (MC dzyuwk).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 大(おほ) (ofo, stem of classical adjective 大(おほ)き (ofoki), modern 大(おお)きい (ōkii, “big”)) + 方(かた) (kata, “direction, way, side”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 學士 (hæwk dzri^X).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 戰鬪 (*jiɛ̀n *təuᴴ). Compare Mandarin 戰鬥 /战斗 (zhàndòu), Korean 전투 (jeontu), Vietnamese chiến đấu.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 數 (MC srjuX|srjuH).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 模 is a daiyōji replacing 摸.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Short for 気(き)障(ざわ)り (kizawari, “disagreeable”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 溜(た)まる (tamaru, “to gather, to accumulate”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 無 (mu-, “without”) + 意味 (imi, “meaning”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese compound 產物 /产物 (srɛn^X mjut, literally “produce + thing”). Compare modern Min Nan reading sán-bu̍t, Cantonese caan² mat⁶.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: By surface analysis, 税務(ぜいむ) (zeimu) + 署(しょ) (-sho).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Ultimately from Middle Chinese 給食 (MC kip zyik, literally “to give, to supply + food, meal”). Sourced from the Chinese work 史記 /史记 (Shǐjì, “Records of the Grand Historian”) completed in 91 BCE.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 緩(ゆる) (yuru, “loose”) + める (-meru, “-ify”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Often taken as from Old Japanese 葬る (haburu). But the epenthesis of う is uncertain. Another form of it is 葬(ほうぶ)る (hōburu). Another theory derive it from 火(ほ) (ho) and 埋(う)むる (umuru), 連体形(れんたいけい) (rentaikei) of 埋(う)む (umu) (modern 埋(う)める (umeru), but is phonologically and morphologically problematic.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Middle Chinese 蝶 (MC thep|dep).
Phonological development: tepu → tefu → tewu → teu → tjoː [tɕoː]

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 装 is a daiyōji replacing 裳.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 衣 (i, “clothing; clothes”) + 類 (rui, “kind; category; group”): literally, “[belonging to] the 'clothes' group [of items]”.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 赤(あか) (aka, “red”) + 字(じ) (ji, “characters”). The “deficit” sense, attested since the Taishō period, relates to the tradition of indicating negative sums in a ledger with red ink. Compare English in the red.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/wau komʉ/ → /wauɡomʉ/ → /wauɡon/ → /wɔːɡoɴ/ → /oːɡoɴ/
From Middle Chinese 黃金 (MC hwang kim, “yellow + metal”).
Compare modern Cantonese wong⁴ gam¹.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/kʷau kimʉ/ → /kʷaukin/ → /kʷɔːkiɴ/ → /koːkiɴ/
From Middle Chinese 黃金 (MC hwang kim, “yellow + metal”).
Compare modern Min Nan reading hông-kim.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Shift from Old Japanese 黃金 (kugane).
Equivalent to a compound of 黄 (ko, combining form of ki, “yellow(-coloured)”) + 金 (kane, “metal”). The kane changes to gane as an instance of rendaku (連濁).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Compound of 黄 (ki, “yellow(-coloured)”) + 金 (kane, “metal”).
The kane changes to gane as an instance of rendaku (連濁).
